back: All activities that move farm produce from the producer to the consumer.
Assembling, grading, processing, packaging, storage, transport, financing, risk bearing, market information, selling.
Controlled: government sets the price or the buyer. Uncontrolled: price set by supply and demand.
Formal: registered, contracts, grading, records (GMB, auctions, abattoirs, supermarkets). Informal: cash sales at roadsides and villages.
Perishability, bulk, seasonality, quality, distance and roads, supply and demand, information, storage, government policy, number of buyers.

front: Roles of the GMB and TIMB
back: GMB: buys, stores and sells grain; strategic reserves. TIMB: registers and regulates tobacco growers, buyers and sales.
A buyer agrees in advance to buy the crop and often supplies inputs and credit repaid from the sale.
Net price = selling price − marketing costs (transport, fees, commission).
